# Machine learning

Models small enough to train inside a box, in plain Kotlin, while you watch. Flow matching carries one 2D or 3D point cloud onto another and hands back the deformation between them; the multi-output regression head it trains is usable on its own. See [Flow Matching](../flow_matching.md).

## flowmatching.kt { #flowmatching-kt }

Flow matching over 2D and 3D point clouds — `flowMatch` trains a velocity field that carries one
distribution onto another, and the field it returns can be sampled, integrated part-way, or drawn.

The idea is small enough to state completely. Pick a point `x0` from where you are starting and a
point `x1` from where you want to end up, and declare that the straight line between them is the
path a particle should take: at time `t` it is at `xt = (1-t)·x0 + t·x1`, travelling at `x1 - x0`.
Now fit a network `v(x, t)` to that velocity by least squares over many random `(x0, x1, t)`
triples. No two straight lines agree where they cross, so the fit cannot reproduce any single one
of them; what it converges to is the *average* velocity through each point at each time, and
integrating that average from `t = 0` to `t = 1` transports the whole starting distribution onto
the whole target one. That is the entire trick, and it is why there is no adversary, no sampler in
the training loop, and nothing to diverge — the loss is a plain regression MSE.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val target = flowSamples(myLine, 600, jitter = 4.0)   // sampled FLine + noise
val field = flowMatch(target, options = FlowMatchOptions(steps = 6000))
val cloud = field.sample(600)                         // fresh points from the same shape
val threads = field.paths(80)                         // the trajectories, as FLines
```

With a `from` cloud supplied it becomes a morph instead of a generator, and then `FlowMatchField.transport`
is the interesting call: it runs the ODE only part-way, so `transport(a, to = 0.5)` is a genuine
half-way shape rather than a vertex-wise average of two point lists.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val morph = flowMatch(to = flowSamples(lineB, 600), from = flowSamples(lineA, 600))
val halfway = morph.transport(flowSamples(lineA, 600), to = 0.5)
```

### Coordinates

Training happens in a normalised frame — the target cloud (both clouds, for a morph) is centred
and isotropically scaled to roughly unit variance — because a Gaussian source has to be
commensurate with the data for any of this to work, and FLine coordinates are usually in the
hundreds. The scaling is a single factor rather than per-axis, so it cannot squash a shape's aspect
ratio. [`FlowMatchField`](machine-learning.md#flowmatching-kt-flowmatchfield) converts at its boundary, so everything you pass in and get back is in the
coordinates you started with.

2D and 3D are distinguished by the data, not by a flag: a cloud whose `z` never varies is trained
as a 2D problem and its points come back on that same `z` plane. Pass `FlowMatchOptions.dimension`
to override. It matters — a 2D shape trained as 3D gets a Gaussian's worth of spread in `z` that
the field then has to learn to collapse.

### What this is not

- **Not a big model.** The default is two hidden layers of 64 `leaky` units trained by RMSProp,
  which is right for a few thousand points in two or three dimensions and nothing like enough for
  images. Training is single-threaded and per-sample (Smile's MLP has no batched matmul), so cost
  scales with `steps × batch`; see the timings in `FlowMatchingTest`.
- **Not able to change topology.** Integrating a velocity field is a continuous invertible map, so
  it cannot tear a loop open or join two strands into one — a flow can only deform. With
  `FlowCoupling.PAIRED` this stops being an abstraction and starts being the dominant error term:
  asking a straight segment to become a closed ring makes the mean landing error fifteen times
  worse than asking a small circle to do it, because the two ends of the segment are pulled to the
  same place and their paths have to cross. Give a closed target a closed source.
- **Not exact.** The field is an average over crossing paths, so samples land *near* the target
  distribution, not on it. Sharp corners smooth off, and thin structure needs more `steps` and more
  `hidden` before it resolves. `FlowMatchField.loss` is the training MSE, which measures the velocity
  fit and not the quality of the samples — judge those by looking, or with `chamferDistance`.
- **Not ordered.** `FlowMatchField.sample` returns an unordered cloud. Recovering an FLine from it is a
  separate problem; `FlowMatchField.transport` sidesteps it by moving points you already have, which
  keeps whatever order they came in.
- **Not conditional.** There is no class label or text prompt input — one field carries one
  distribution onto one other.

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">VectorMLP</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">outputs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">hidden</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">IntArray</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">intArrayOf</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">96</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="mi">96</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">activation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;tanh&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MultilayerPerceptron</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">&#42;</span><span class="nf">mlpLayers</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">inputs</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">hidden</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">outputs</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">activation</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/flowmatching/#L106)

A multi-output regression MLP, which is the one thing Smile's own `smile.regression.MLP` will not do — it fixes the output layer at a single neuron and `predict` returns a `Double`.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Width of the input vector. |

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">activation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The hidden activation, kept because `exportWeights` has to name it and Smile does not. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">predict</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">into</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">outputs</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/flowmatching/#L117) | Runs the network forward, writing `outputs` values into `into`, which is returned. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">accumulate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">y</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/flowmatching/#L132) | Adds one sample's gradient to the batch, returning that sample's squared error. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">step</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">batchSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/flowmatching/#L152) | Applies the accumulated gradient of a batch of `batchSize` samples and advances the clock. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">configure</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">learningRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">momentum</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">rho</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1e</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">7</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/flowmatching/#L158) | Configures RMSProp, momentum and learning rate together, the combination `flowMatch` uses. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">configure</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">learningRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">TimeFunction</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">momentum</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">rho</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1e</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">7</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/flowmatching/#L170) | As `configure`, but with a learning-rate *schedule* — `TimeFunction.linear(from, steps, to)` and friends, indexed by the `step` count. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">parameterCount</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/flowmatching/#L177) | How many parameters — weights plus biases — the network is fitting. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">exportWeights</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MlpWeights</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/flowmatching/#L210) | A flat snapshot of every weight and bias, in the layout [`MlpWeights`](machine-learning.md#neuralparticles-kt-mlpweights) documents — which is what `afield.stdlib.glsl` turns into a shader. |

Constants: `EULER`, `MIDPOINT`.

The knobs `flowMatch` takes, bundled so that a call that only wants to change one of them does not have to name the rest positionally.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">steps</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Gradient steps to take. The dominant cost and the dominant quality lever. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">batch</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples per gradient step. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">hidden</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">IntArray</span></code> | Hidden layer widths. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">activation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Hidden activation: `leaky`, `relu`, `tanh`, `sigmoid` or `linear`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">learningRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | RMSProp learning rate at the first step. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">finalLearningRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Learning rate at the last step, decayed linearly from `learningRate`; null to hold it constant. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">momentum</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Momentum, or 0 to disable. **Leave this at 0 unless `rho` is also 0.** |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rho</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | RMSProp decay, or 0 to fall back to plain SGD. See `momentum` before changing either. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">timeFeatures</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many `sin`/`cos` octaves of the time input the network sees, on top of raw `t`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">coupling</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FlowCoupling</span></code> | How `x0` is paired with `x1`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">jitter</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Standard deviation of noise added to each drawn data point, in input coordinates. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">seed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Seed for the training draws. `null` takes an unpredictable one. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">dimension</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Override the inferred 2-or-3 dimensionality. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">onProgress</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Called every `progressEvery` steps with the step index and the running mean loss. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">progressEvery</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How often `onProgress` fires. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">equals</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">other</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/flowmatching/#L425) |  |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">hashCode</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/flowmatching/#L428) |  |

### FlowMatchField { #flowmatching-kt-flowmatchfield }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">FlowMatchField</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">dimension</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">net</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">VectorMLP</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">timeFeatures</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">frame</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FlowFrame</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">sourcePoints</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Array</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">losses</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/flowmatching/#L798)

A trained velocity field, as returned by `flowMatch` — the thing you integrate.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |

| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">loss</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">count</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/flowmatching/#L813) | Mean training loss over the last `count` steps — steadier to read than `loss` alone. |

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">MlpWeights</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">inputs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">outputs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">hidden</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">IntArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">activation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MlpActivation</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">flat</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatArray</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/stdlib/neuralparticles/#L59)

Taking a small trained network to the GPU: [`MlpWeights`](machine-learning.md#neuralparticles-kt-mlpweights) is a flat, layer-major snapshot of a multilayer perceptron's weights, and `MlpWeights.glsl` emits a GLSL function that evaluates the same network out of a storage buffer.

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">dwellCycles</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How long a particle rests on the target once it arrives, as a multiple of the travel time. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">phaseSpread</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How far apart in the cycle the particles start, as a fraction of a whole cycle. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">pointSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Point size in pixels. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sourceColor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec4</span></code> | Colour a particle leaves the source with. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetColor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec4</span></code> | Colour it arrives at the target with. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">intensity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Overall brightness. With additive blending this is the exposure control. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">arrivalBias</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How strongly a particle's brightness is weighted toward the end of its journey, 0..1. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">viewScale</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Half-height of the visible region, in the field's normalised units. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">viewCenter</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vector2f</span></code> | Centre of the visible region, in the field's normalised units. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">flipY</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether to negate `y` on the way to clip space. On by default. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sourceJitter</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Gaussian spread, in the field's normalised units, added to each particle's source point. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">randomSeed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | Seed for the source draw, so a scene reloads identically. |
